//: THE DEAD COME FOR YOU WITH THEIR ARMS OUT. An ADDITIVE hold, not a motion: it raises both shoulders to roughly 80 degrees of forward flexion, leaves a few degrees of elbow bend, and lets the hands droop, and then does almost nothing for the rest of its cycle. The slow counter-phased drift (76<->82 on one shoulder, 81<->75 on the other) exists only so the pose is not a statue -- an outstretched arm that is perfectly still reads as a rig that has frozen, which is the exact failure the notes in anim.cpp and avatar.cpp describe. Additive on purpose, so whatever swing the body already has survives underneath: on an NPC that is the procedural swingAmp sine (MobSystem::UpdateAnimation), on a clip-driven rig it is the walk/run arm cycle, and in both cases the arms shamble while they reach instead of being pinned. Rotations are pure X, positive = backward/down (anim.cpp's convention, the same sign the walk clip's arm tracks use), so no part of this clip depends on which way the lateral axis points. Played by MobSystem::UpdateAnimation for any def with a `chaseClip`, weight-ramped by Mob::chasePose_ -- it is NOT started or stopped per tick, the weight is what moves.
name: reach
